request_bounds_basis.details: The actor bills per company looked up, and both `companies[]` (URLs) and `searches[]` (names to search) are looked up (experiments/hiring-actor-benchmark-2026-08-01/schemas/harvestapi__linkedin-company.input.json; compileHarvestCompanyDetailsInput bills companies + searches). The engine sends one LinkedIn URL in `companies` and never `searches`, so `searches` is refused outright and the purchase is one company.
request_bounds_basis.jobs: Billed rows are maxItems per job title per location: the actor runs once per `jobTitles` entry, and maxItems applies per title and location input (harvestapi__linkedin-job-search.input.json). `jobTitles`, `locations` and `geoIds` (the other location filter) are therefore bounded, and `maxItems` is mandatory. `company`, `industryIds`, `workplaceType`, `employmentType`, `experienceLevel`, `salary`, `postedLimit`, `sortBy`, `under10Applicants` and `easyApply` are filters that narrow each search, and `page` only chooses where a search starts, so none of them multiplies the rows. They are left unbounded, and the gate-pinned maxTotalChargeUsd caps the run either way.

read_plan.enforced_by: reads.request_limits.max_reads_per_actor (admit_discovery_smoke refuses `read_allocation`; the worker's read plan uses each actor's share), inside the shared cap of 5
read_plan.slow_job_search: a job search needing two status reads keeps its dataset read and defers its receipt; company details keeps its two
read_plan.deferred: any receipt the allocation leaves no read for (normally the company details'): committed maximum held, listed by scripts/test-project/smoke-reconciliation.sql, closed only by reconcile_discovery_smoke_operation
